issue_context.title: "Play first item in m3u and pls playlists when casting" (pull #70047) breaks playback of some playlists
issue_context.body:
### The problem

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/70047 breaks radio stream playback for some m3u8 playlist streams. pychromecast fails with a "Load media failed with code 104(MEDIA_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED) for item 1" error. The HA log has a generic "Please make sure the URL is: Reachable from the cast device and either a publicly resolvable hostname or an IP address" error.

Modifying the URL to not end with .m3u8 by appending a useless parameter will make it work again as it passes the playlist URL instead of the first stream inside.

Broken URL:

https://rthkaudio2-lh.akamaihd.net/i/radio2_1@355865/master.m3u8

```
#EXTM3U
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:PROGRAM-ID=1,BANDWIDTH=54000,CODECS="mp4a.40.2"
https://rthkaudio2-lh.akamaihd.net/i/radio2_1@355865/index_56_a-p.m3u8?sd=10&rebase=on
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:PROGRAM-ID=1,BANDWIDTH=54000,CODECS="mp4a.40.2"
https://rthkaudio2-lh.akamaihd.net/i/radio2_1@355865/index_56_a-b.m3u8?sd=10&rebase=on
```

It tries to play "https://rthkaudio2-lh.akamaihd.net/i/radio2_1@355865/index_56_a-p.m3u8?sd=10&rebase=on" but fails.

Modified working URL:

https://rthkaudio2-lh.akamaihd.net/i/radio2_1@355865/master.m3u8?a


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.5.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.4.7

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Google Cast

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cast/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
Broken:

media_content_id: https://rthkaudio2-lh.akamaihd.net/i/radio2_1@355865/master.m3u8
media_content_type: music
extra:
  title: RTHK 2

Working:

media_content_id: https://rthkaudio2-lh.akamaihd.net/i/radio2_1@355865/master.m3u8?a
media_content_type: music
extra:
  title: RTHK 2
```

comments:
Hey there @emontnemery, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`cast`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L157) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I'm seeing something similar but get a different error message. I have the following script that started failing with latest version of HA (2022.05).

```yaml
radio_national_bathroom:
  alias: "Stream Radio National in bathroom"
  sequence:
    - service: media_player.play_media
      target:
        entity_id: media_player.bathroom_speaker
      data:
        media_content_id: "https://abcradiolivehls-lh.akamaihd.net/i/rnnsw_1@327290/master.m3u8"
        media_content_type: "music"
```

Error in logs:

> 2022-05-09 14:23:20 ERROR (Thread-10) [homeassistant.components.cast.media_player] Failed to cast media https://abcradiolivehls-lh.akamaihd.net/i/rnnsw_1@327290/index_24_a-p.m3u8?sd=10&rebase=on. Please make sure the URL is: Reachable from the cast device and either a publicly resolvable hostname or an IP address

> I'm seeing something similar but get a different error message.

It is the same error. MEDIA_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED is from the pychromecast debug log. The normal HA log shows "Please make sure the URL is: Reachable from the cast device and either a publicly resolvable hostname or an IP address". I've edited the first post to show this error as users are more likely to be searching for that.

Looks like your station is also an akamaihd.net hosted one. I'm not sure why the cast receiver rejects those playlists. As a temporary workaround, add ?a to the end of the media_content_id i.e. ""https://abcradiolivehls-lh.akamaihd.net/i/rnnsw_1@327290/master.m3u8?a".

> As a temporary workaround, add `?a` to the end of the media_content_id

This worked, thanks for the pointer.

This is a regression from PR #70047 which gave chromecasts rudimentary support for playing web radio streams from m3u[8] and pls playlists which are otherwise not supported.
The problem is that HLS is *also* using m3u8, and there's there's no trivial way to determine if the m3u8 playlist is an HLS playlist or not. The approach takes was too simplistic as it will not detect HLS version 1 playlists as HLS.

PR #71564 improves HLS detection by also considering the content type.
